verdicts.note: Attacked as overstated: she has held the top job only since April 6, 2026 (S5, S6). But she is the sitting sheriff, chief criminal deputy from 2023 and a sergeant from 2022 (S1, S2), running on continuity against a line deputy. -1 rather than -2 already reflects the short tenure; high confidence fits a documented record.

Attacked toward +1: her most specific policy statements favor treatment over jail ('outreach programs ... access to treatment rather than jail', drug court, S5) and a treatment-linked re-entry program (S9). Against that, her listed priorities are keeping drugs off the streets, crimes against children, more detectives and raising jail staffing (S7, S9), which is pole_a's staffing and enforcement. The two are balanced, so 0 at medium, a genuine mix, holds.

'Be very budget conscious and stay within our budget' (S7), buying used patrol vehicles and warning that grants are not 'free money' (S9). These are restraint statements within her own office, with no audit agenda, so -1 rather than -2. Medium is right for two consistent sources.

Deputy since 2007 with no supervisory or elected record (S1, S3). He runs as the change candidate, saying trust in the office has 'deteriorated' (S1). His 19 years inside the office keep this at +1, not +2.

Direction is right: he blames Olympia's 'alternatives to incarceration' for a crime surge, wants proactive policing and calls jail staffing the top issue (S2). But his key line is hedged: the deterrent 'can, at times, be incarceration ... even though there are other alternatives' (S2). It concedes alternatives instead of rejecting them. All of it comes from one source, his campaign site. He proposes nothing on repeat-offender prosecution, mandatory treatment or encampments, the fuller pole_a markers. A clear lean, not the full pole.

Inapplicable evidence. The reform axis is about money and power in politics: refusing PAC money, term limits, dark-money bans, RCV, direct democracy. His points are that trust in the sheriff's office has deteriorated, that staffing problems come from leadership, and that he would practice 'servant leadership' and transparency (S1, S2, S6). Those are internal management and morale, not structural political reform. The dossier records nothing on campaign money or electoral reform.
